human_pressure.one_screen_brief: 8101 added a pre-action actor-substitution gate, but current positive authorization can still match only role/from/to/reason/authority facts. Latest dogfood shows that the runtime's classified cause of a fallback matters to whether a substitute actor should inherit authority. Extend the existing 8101 seam with one opaque runtime-supplied cause_classification fact. Ailuros must not map provider/backend error strings into causes. Positive ALLOW becomes sufficient only when at least one matched ALLOW policy explicitly constrains cause_classification; legacy broad ALLOW policies that omit it must converge to REQUIRE_REVIEW. Existing BLOCK, REQUIRE_REVIEW, WARN/SANITIZE fail-closed behavior and tool-call governance must remain unchanged.
human_pressure.goal: Require explicit policy authorization of the runtime-supplied substitution cause before a replacement actor can receive an ALLOW decision.
non_goals: Do not build provider/backend error classification inside Ailuros.
Do not add a fallback router, retry manager, actor registry, trust score or model/provider reputation system.
Do not create a cause taxonomy enum or universal failure ontology from the current dogfood sample.
Do not redesign the Policy schema, DecisionResolver or GovernanceDecisionType.
Do not integrate EverRun-specific backend strings into Ailuros core.
red_lines: Ailuros must never derive cause_classification from reason, provider name, model name, exception text or backend error text.
Only a matched ALLOW policy that explicitly binds cause_classification may authorize substitution.
A legacy matched ALLOW policy omitting cause_classification must no longer be sufficient for ALLOW on this path.
Unknown classification may be authorized only if policy explicitly matches unknown.
Ailuros still does not select, start, retry or orchestrate replacement actors.
do_not_misread: cause_classification is an opaque policy fact supplied by the integrating runtime/adapter.
The existing free-form reason remains preserved and opaque; it is not replaced by cause_classification.
This intentionally tightens only the positive ALLOW branch of actor substitution.
Append the optional cause_classification parameter after the existing metadata parameter to preserve positional caller compatibility.

machine_core.goal: Extend ActorSubstitutionContext and AilurosRuntime.before_actor_substitution with optional cause_classification='unknown', and require explicit cause binding in matched ALLOW policy evidence before returning ALLOW.
acceptance: ActorSubstitutionContext contains cause_classification as an opaque string with default 'unknown'.
before_actor_substitution preserves existing arguments and appends cause_classification after metadata with default 'unknown'.
ACTOR_SUBSTITUTION_REQUESTED payload and GovernanceDecision metadata include the exact runtime-supplied cause_classification.
reason remains preserved as an independent opaque string.
A matched ALLOW policy that explicitly constrains cause_classification can return ALLOW and allowed=true.
A matched ALLOW policy that omits cause_classification converges to REQUIRE_REVIEW and allowed=false.
A mismatched cause classification produces no positive authorization and results in REQUIRE_REVIEW.
An explicit policy matching cause_classification='unknown' may authorize an unknown classification.
Existing BLOCK remains BLOCK; REQUIRE_REVIEW remains REQUIRE_REVIEW; WARN and SANITIZE remain non-authorizing and converge to REQUIRE_REVIEW.
Existing tool-call policy behavior remains unchanged.
No provider/backend-specific classifier or cause taxonomy is introduced.
All focused and full validation commands pass.
red_lines: Do not change GovernanceDecisionType, DecisionResolver, Policy schema or PolicyEngine.
Do not infer cause_classification from reason or any actor/provider/model identifier.
Do not add provider-specific or EverRun-specific branching.
Do not create a new before_actor_substitution_v2 API.
Do not authorize a substitution merely because a legacy ALLOW policy matched role/from/to/reason/authority.
Do not execute or orchestrate fallback actors inside Ailuros.
failure_semantics: Missing cause_classification becomes the explicit value 'unknown'; it is not guessed from reason.
Positive authorization without an explicit matched policy constraint on cause_classification is insufficient and must REQUIRE_REVIEW.
A policy may explicitly authorize 'unknown'; this is a conscious policy decision rather than a default.
Explicit BLOCK still blocks regardless of positive authorization tightening.
WARN and SANITIZE remain non-authorizing for actor substitution.
Provider/model availability and backend error interpretation remain external runtime concerns.
invariants: Actor identities and cause classification remain opaque runtime-supplied strings.
Only explicit ALLOW with explicit cause binding yields allowed=true.
No-policy actor substitution remains REQUIRE_REVIEW as established by 8101.
The global DecisionResolver no-policy behavior remains unchanged.
Existing tool-call runtime enforcement remains unchanged.
Ailuros does not own fallback selection or execution.

must_check: The change extends the existing actor-substitution seam rather than creating a parallel API or framework.
cause_classification is present in ActorSubstitutionContext, request evidence and decision metadata.
No code maps reason/provider/model/error strings into cause_classification.
A matched ALLOW policy must explicitly constrain cause_classification before ALLOW is returned.
A legacy ALLOW policy without cause_classification is downgraded to REQUIRE_REVIEW.
An explicit policy matching cause_classification='unknown' can intentionally authorize unknown.
BLOCK, REQUIRE_REVIEW, WARN/SANITIZE and no-policy fail-closed actor-substitution behavior remain correct.
DecisionResolver, Policy schema, PolicyEngine and GovernanceDecisionType are unchanged.
Tool-call runtime governance still passes unchanged.
No forbidden files changed and every validation command passed.
reject_if: Ailuros derives cause_classification from reason, exception text, provider, model or backend-specific strings.
A legacy ALLOW policy omitting cause_classification can still authorize actor substitution.
Missing classification silently inherits authorization from reason or actor identity.
A new cause enum/taxonomy, fallback router, actor registry, trust score or provider reputation mechanism is introduced.
DecisionResolver global semantics, Policy schema, PolicyEngine or GovernanceDecisionType are changed.
A new actor-substitution API is introduced instead of extending the existing one.
Ailuros selects, starts, retries or orchestrates the substitute actor.
Existing BLOCK/REQUIRE_REVIEW/WARN/SANITIZE or tool-call semantics regress.
Validation fails or forbidden files change.
